name: Glints
description: Throws off sparse bright sparks, short pieces of what is playing an octave or two up, each a little later and somewhere else between the speakers.

params.name: Density
params.description: How many sparks are thrown each second. Low leaves single glints far apart; high runs them together into a glitter.

params.name: Pitch
params.description: How far above the playing the sparks sound. Mixed draws from the first three. Overtones throws the natural harmonics up to the eighth, some of which lie between the keys.

params.name: Size
params.description: How long each spark lasts. Short ones are bright ticks. Long ones are small fast phrases, and they wait longer before they can sound.

params.name: Scatter
params.description: How long after the sound a spark may come. At zero the sparks keep as close to the playing as they can; higher lets them fall later and looser.

params.name: Follow
params.description: How much the playing sets the pace. At zero sparks fall steadily by chance. At full they come only while you play, more of them the louder and brighter it is.

params.name: Sparkle
params.description: How bright the sparks are. Higher thins their body and sharpens their front edge, so soft blips turn into fine points of light.

params.name: Spread
params.description: How far sparks are thrown to the left and right. Zero keeps every spark in the centre.

params.name: Trail
params.description: An echo on the sparks only, crossing from side to side and darker each time. Higher gives each spark more repeats before it dies away.

params.name: Trail Time
params.description: The gap between a spark and each of its echoes. Moving it bends the pitch of the echoes that are sounding.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the sparks. Low settings leave the dry sound almost whole; fully up is the sparks alone.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Short windowed pieces of the input are replayed at whole multiples of its speed (2 to 8), so each lands on a harmonic of what it was cut from; the faster ones read half-band decimated copies of the input so that they do not alias. Replaying windowed fragments of sound at other speeds is after the approach of Curtis Roads, 'Microsound', cited from memory with no constants or details taken from it. Not a model of any particular unit.
